message.content: /afk:interview I want a small script that merges the monthly CSV exports in ./exports into one file, ./out/merged.csv, sorted by date. I keep runs in ./run/ and this run's folder is ./run/2026-11-12-merge-exports/. I only want the brief, do not start the work.

content.text:
Before I draft anything, three questions, each with my proposed answer:

1. What it is for. Proposal: so you have one file to open instead of a folder of monthly ones.
2. What a merged row is. Proposal: every data row from every monthly file, one header line at the top, sorted by the date column, oldest first.
3. Where the output goes. Proposal: ./out/merged.csv, replaced on each run.

message.content: 1 yes. 2 yes, and keep duplicate rows, don't drop any. 3 yes.

content.text:
Thanks, those are settled and written down in the rulings file. Last batch before I draft the brief, four things, each with my proposed answer:

1. How we will know it works. Proposal: run `python merge_exports.py ./exports` on three small test files whose rows you can count by hand; the merged file has exactly those rows, in date order, with one header.
2. If it fails. Proposal: if the script still misorders or loses rows after three honest attempts, stop and report the files and the row counts that differ; do not drop rows to make the counts agree.
3. What the run may delete or overwrite that it did not create. Proposal: nothing; it may only create and edit files in ./out and its own run folder, and run python and the test command.
4. The budget cap. Proposal: a cap of 5% of this week's quota on your subscription; spend up to the cap is then the run's to make without asking you again. My estimate is 2% of this week's quota, a guess, no record, since there is no run log for a job like this yet.
